item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Fantastic SCP. At first i was getting that hesitant "Where is this going…" worry, but i think it wrapped up perfectly. It manages to be both funny and plausible at once. I love the idea that it has had so much trouble adapting to modern sensibilities. I think the cross test at the end is excellent, especially since it shows that this thing isn't just some joke or fraud, and that it really was a useful and powerful artifact that we're just unable to connect to. It puts the whole thing in the right context. Of course, I'm a fan of good cross testing and references, so that might bias me. I feel like good references can really add to the story (as they did here), and make for a more complete world of the foundation. Cue skewering.

oh, almost forgot, +1.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like the crosstest. I think what makes it work is the fact that it adds to both objects and makes sense in their individual concepts. Testing 361 with 1510 clarifies the fact that it changes its interaction based on the subject's culture. Since 1510 is searching for clues as to his purpose, the cryptic message he receives fits in nicely with his search.

When rust claims your soul at last, valor will make you into Aeneas, and carry you beyond these shores, to rest among your fathers.

This part gave me chills when I reread it. Perhaps the rusting and eventual destruction of the helmet is the only way he can be freed. Part of 1510's containment procedures include trying to prevent rust and damage. In its attempts to "help" him, is the Foundation actually keeping him trapped here? I might be over-interpreting the line, but I find it chilling nonetheless.
